title: Customer Service
text: And so, for that reason, I brought Father and the others along to Panda’s village. How nostalgic, I say. One way or another, ever since Panda and Father grew close, this village has become a place we visit more and more often. Depending on the circumstances, it’s even become something of a leisurely getaway spot, indeed. In the previous loop, Father used to come here to relax and unwind too. It seemed like he alternated between mooching off Big Sister’s village and this one.
“Ohh… so many pandas. It’s like some kind of dream place.”
I could see Father’s eyes positively sparkling. He always looks so delighted like this.
“There’s even a bamboo grove! It really feels like the sort of place you’d imagine! Waah… what a dream come true.”
As Father walked toward the village looking all around, a village panda near the entrance noticed us.
“Oh my? Travelers, perhaps?”
The village panda addressed us with a somewhat wary air.
“Ah, yes. We’re travelers—we heard there was a village here and decided to stop by.”

Father handled the village panda with his business smile. The village panda looked Father up and down, then turned its gaze to me, Elephant, and Older Sister. After that, it stared intently at Father. Probably wondering why on earth a human would come here. Apparently, demi-humans and beastmen also tend to feel some strange sensation upon first meeting Father, aside from that suspicion. According to Father, it’s likely something to do with the power of the Shield’s sacred weapon or some such.
“I see… welcome, then. It must have been quite a journey to get here. Travelers, we can’t offer much of a warm welcome, but please, rest easy in the village.”
“Yes, thank you very much.”
With that exchange of greetings, the village panda hurried off toward the grandfather panda’s house. Presumably to report that some unfamiliar folks had shown up.
“So this is Lars’s hometown… honestly, there’s no other way to put it—there really are a ton of Lars’s kin here.”
Elephant nodded, looking around, seeming convinced.
“Ohh, I wonder if this village has any local specialty sake?”

Older Sister seemed preoccupied with sake, as always. I recalled her searching for sake here before too. I think there was indeed some brewed locally. If we asked, surely they’d sell us some? Then again, now that I thought about it, I’d never actually come to this village without Panda along. No telling how things would go, but no matter—there shouldn’t be any real problems, I say.
“Man, for a panda lover, this place is basically paradise, huh.”
“And what about you, Naofumi-chan?”
“I mean, sure, pandas are cute, right? Though apparently zoo pandas have pretty sharp-looking eyes most of the time—but whenever I went, I never saw that kind of expression on them.”

Father regaled us with a story about seeing pandas at the zoo. Apparently, after eating bamboo, one had looked like it was waving at him, which he’d found delightful. Also, apparently a panda had come up to sniff at him through the glass, and everyone had swarmed for the photo opportunity, shoving him right out of line.
“So yeah, at the zoo I never really got to see them up close like that.”

A cheerful little anecdote from Father. As for me, whenever I went on dates with pigs, I always seemed to end up watching the pig far more than the actual animals. I knew perfectly well that if I kept staring at the animals too long, the pig would get sulky. Honestly, at that rate there’s hardly any difference between an amusement park and a zoo—it’s basically a pig farm, I say. It seemed like Father was having a much more enjoyable time than I ever had, which stirred up a bit of envy in me. And so, chatting like this, we wandered the panda village in search of an establishment—an inn, a tavern, that sort of thing. Even small villages tend to have a tavern or two, serving as a communal gathering spot for the villagers. I’d been to this village a few times before, so I had a decent grasp of the terrain, but for Father and the others, this was their first time. Still, since we usually stayed at Panda’s house as our base, now that we’d come as ordinary travelers, checking out the tavern seemed the thing to do. We stepped into a cozy little tavern. It likely doubled as an inn too—ask nicely, and they’d probably let us stay the night.
“Looks like Elmelo-san won’t be able to fit in… though it is bigger than the taverns in Melromarc.”
Elephant, being an oversized beastman, needed a correspondingly large tavern to fit into.
“Don’t worry about it. I’m used to sleeping outdoors.”
“Even so, you know…”
“Ohh~”

And so, while our lodging plans remained undecided, we stood outside the tavern chatting when Panda’s foster father approached. A peacock beastman. Well, having some familiarity with him from the previous loop as well, I recognized him readily as Panda’s foster father.
“Good afternoon. It’s quite rare indeed for travelers to visit this village.”
“Ah, good afternoon. Yes, we heard there was a village here and decided to stop by.”
Father responded to Panda’s foster father’s greeting with a smile.
“So then, travelers, what business brings you here? If you’re in some kind of trouble, I’d be happy to lend an ear.”

Apparently, Panda’s foster father served as the village’s customer service and diplomatic liaison of sorts. He’d ask travelers their business, judge whether they posed a threat, and if it turned out to be commercial in nature, handle the negotiations accordingly. Father seemed to have sensed as much too, glancing at the rest of us before responding on our behalf with his business smile toward Panda’s foster father.

“Well, half of it is simple curiosity, and the other half—we heard there was a formidable warrior living in this village, and we thought we might get the chance to speak with them a little. Ah, please don’t be alarmed. We have absolutely no intention of picking a fight.”
Later, Father would tell me he’d judged it better to be upfront rather than spin some clumsy excuse.

“Hmm… I have no idea of any warrior in this village so formidable that travelers would hear tell of them. I’d like to know a bit more—where exactly did you hear such a rumor, and just who might this person be?”
“Well, it was just a rumor, really—if you’re asking who told us, it was merely something we overheard in the nearest town. It’s all quite uncertain, honestly.”

Ohh… there was Father’s business-customer-service mode in full swing. He deflected Panda’s foster father’s attempt to pin down the source of the rumor with a vague answer. I would have been perfectly willing to testify myself, but Father signaled me with his hand beforehand to hold my tongue, so I kept quiet.
“Going out of your way to verify a mere rumor—my, how diligent of you.”
Panda’s foster father responded with crackling wariness. It seemed he’d seen through the true intent behind Father’s evasiveness.
“Ohh~”
“Hmm…”
Older Sister and Elephant seemed to have sensed the tension too, and chose to hold their tongues, watching how things would unfold.
“As for the content of the rumor—apparently, long ago, this person was quite the formidable fighter, but has since retired and now lives here in this village.”
“That would make them quite elderly indeed. They may well have already passed away.”
An indirect way of saying he had no intention of introducing anyone. Was this a move to keep Father from meeting Panda’s grandfather?
“Is that so? Well, if that’s the case, wouldn’t there at least be some tale told of them in the village? I’d be glad to offer a prayer at their grave, if nothing else.”

Here, Father pressed further still. Panda’s foster father’s eyes seemed to narrow just slightly. I’d always thought of him as a gentle, child-loving sort, but apparently he had this side to him as well.
“Waah, travelers~?”

Just then, a little baby panda peeked out to look at us. Noticing the voice, Father smiled and gave a small wave. Panda’s foster father, as if signaling caution, ruffled his tail feathers and seemed to be trying to usher the child away. Father, sensing this too, nodded in understanding—no need to be wary, we mean no harm. Hmm… without Panda along, the wariness here felt awfully strong, and it didn’t seem like the conversation was going anywhere. Or… was it actually progressing, somehow?
